newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian steelworkers stage 24 hour strike.
newsitem.headline: Australian steelworkers stage 24 hour strike.

text.p: Three thousand Australian steelworkers on Friday staged a snap 24-hour strike in protest at the planned closure of the country's oldest steelworks in the industrial city of Newcastle.
"Of the 3,000, only four people voted against the strike," the Australian Workers Union's Newcastle Secretary Maurie Rudd told Reuters.

Australia's biggest listed company, The Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd (BHP), on Tuesday announced it would close the 82-year-old steelworks by 1999 as part of a rationalisation of its steel division.
BHP said it would lay off 2,500 workers at Newcastle, 120 km (73 miles) north of Sydney, at the foot of the coal-rich Hunter Valley.
The Newcastle steelworkers plan next week to ask the country's peak union body, the Australian Council of Trade Unions, to stage a national strike in protest at the closure.
